valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 21 Nov 2026. (1) Business: one business, a life insurer (Janashakthi Life), plus a 25% equity-accounted stake in First Capital Holdings (a primary dealer and investment group in the same parent group), so one sector beta, life insurance. (2)–(3) An insurer, so the sector's levered beta is used without relevering. Damodaran's emerging-markets file (betaEmerg) couldn't be opened from this run (pages.stern.nyu.edu blocked); his January 2026 global Insurance (Life) levered beta is 0.80 (143 firms; unlevered 0.52), from a web-search extract. (4) Local 5-year betas: only one found (StockAnalysis 0.49); a second and third source weren't available, and the share is closely held (19.97% public float, 8,777 public holders), so the local figure is noted but not relied on. (5) Higher of (3) and (4): 0.80. (6) Within 0.3–2. (7)–(8) Put into the calculator and shown as the Required return tile. Refresh in January 2027 with the emerging-markets figure.

valuationInputs.name: Cost of equity
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (21 Nov 2026): 8.24% + 0.80 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 16.5%, ±1.5 points. Replaces the hand-set 19% / 17.5% / 16% of 13 Nov. No WACC: an insurer is valued on equity.

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 0% / 0.4% / 0.4% dividend growth for the next five years; supported 0.4% (share of profit kept × ROE, FY 2025: 2.0% × 20.5%). All within 2 pts.
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py on FY 2025, when 98% of profit was paid out (Rs 3.40bn of Rs 3.47bn). Dividend growth is capped at the supported rate. Residual income lets book value grow only by the profit kept (40%), and after year 5 every method pays out 1 − g ÷ ROE, so long-run growth of 4–6% is paid for by retained profit. Premiums grew 31% in 2025 and 20.9% in nine months of 2026 and the life fund rose Rs 2.89bn before the surplus transfer in 2025 (note 18.3), which supports future surpluses, but none of that growth is assumed in the next five years' dividend.
